name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+12 district with incumbent Brian Babin on the ballot
Overwhelming fundraising edge: Babin $1.16M raised vs. Hart $24K
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 4-6%
No public polling or expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: A double-digit Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger with minimal resources leave little evidence of a contest. Markets and fundamentals align on a comfortable Babin win.
model.watch: A sudden influx of Democratic outside spending or surprise polling showing a single-digit race would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 36th District, anchored in East Texas, leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Brian Babin is seeking another term after being renominated. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised about $1.16 million and holding more than $900,000 on hand, while Democrat Rhonda Hart has raised roughly $24,000. No public polls track the race, and no major expert ratings list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Hart only a small chance of an upset, and the district's fundamentals point the same way: a double-digit Republican lean, an incumbent advantage, and a favorable environment for the party. The forecast expects Babin to win by a wide margin, with residual uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive contest. Hart would need a dramatic shift in attention or resources to change the picture.
